title: Longitudinal SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccine immunogenicity in inflammatory bowel disease in relation to anti-TNF therapy and age: a prospective cohort study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) on immunomodulatory therapy may respond less well to vaccination. This study aimed to evaluate the immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in IBD patients over 12 months.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This single-centre, prospective cohort study followed adults with IBD who received mRNA vaccine under the Austrian national programme. All 53 participants were infection-naive and twice-vaccinated, with follow-up at 3, 6 and 12 months.
analysis.methods: Two doses of mRNA vaccine were administered 28 days apart, with a third dose given 6-12 months after the first. S1-RBD IgG, live-virus 50% neutralisation titres (NT50) against wild-type, Delta, Omicron BA.1 and BA.2, and IFN-γ ELISpot responses were measured at baseline and after 3, 6 and 12 months. Associations with anti-TNF therapy and age were analysed using rank-based longitudinal models and mixed-effects models adjusted for age and sex.
analysis.main_results: All 53 twice-vaccinated, infection-naive patients seroconverted at 3 months. The geometric mean (GM) S1-RBD IgG peaked at 3 months (465.7 BAU/ml) and fell by 6 months (124.8 BAU/ml). At 6 months, the adjusted geometric mean ratio versus other therapy was 0.31 (95% CI 0.20-0.49) for S1-RBD IgG and 0.22 (0.12-0.41) for wild-type NT50. Each additional year of age was associated with 2.4% lower wild-type NT50 (0.976 per year, 95% CI 0.962-0.990).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Anti-TNF therapy and higher age within a relatively young cohort were associated with lower and shorter-lived humoral responses, while cellular responses appeared comparatively preserved. These exploratory associations need confirmation in larger cohorts with clinical endpoints.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the need for monitoring vaccine responses in IBD patients on anti-TNF therapy and highlight the potential impact of age on immunogenicity. They also suggest that cellular immunity may remain robust despite reduced humoral responses.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its single-centre design and relatively small sample size. The evidence is moderate as it is based on an observational cohort study with no clinical endpoints.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunogenicity of SARS-CoV-2 mRNA vaccines in adults with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) over 12 months, focusing on the impact of anti-TNF therapy and age. All 53 participants seroconverted after the first two doses, with peak IgG levels at 3 months and a significant decline by 6 months. Anti-TNF therapy was linked to faster waning of humoral responses, while age was associated with reduced neutralisation titres. Cellular responses, measured by IFN-γ ELISpot, remained preserved. The study highlights the importance of monitoring vaccine effectiveness in IBD patients on immunomodulatory therapies and suggests that age may influence immune response. However, the findings are exploratory and require validation in larger cohorts with clinical outcomes. The evidence is moderate due to the observational design and limited sample size.

title: Tracking SARS-CoV-2: Molecular epidemiology and surveillance in Health Region VIII, Buenos Aires, Argentina (2020–2021)

analysis.scope_and_question: Describe the classical and molecular epidemiology of SARS-CoV-2 in Health Region VIII, Buenos Aires Province, Argentina during 2020–2021, focusing on viral introductions, transmission dynamics, genetic diversity, and substitution rates.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A single observational study analyzed 120,421 respiratory samples from patients with acute respiratory infection in HRVIII during 2020–2021, and obtained complete genome or partial spike gene sequences for phylogenetic analyses.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: SARS-CoV-2 positivity was higher in 2020 (37.4%) than in 2021 (31.9%), with travelers showing higher rates in 2020 and residents in 2021. The first wave (EW 37, 2020) was dominated by lineages B.1.1.33, N.3, and B.1.499; early 2021 saw a resurgence of N.5 and emerging Alpha and Lambda variants; the second wave (EW 20) featured cocirculation of Gamma and Lambda, later displaced by Delta after EW 31. Estimated substitution rates ranged from 2.4 × 10−4 to 6.8 × 10−4 substitutions/site/year.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report limitations or evidence gaps.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This study underscores the importance of integrating genomic surveillance into public health systems to monitor emerging variants and support timely response strategies.

analysis.summary_en: A descriptive study of 120,421 respiratory samples from Health Region VIII, Buenos Aires, Argentina, during 2020–2021 examined SARS-CoV-2 epidemiology through genome sequencing. Positivity rates were higher in 2020 than 2021, with travelers initially more affected. Lineage dynamics shifted from B.1.1.33, N.3, and B.1.499 in the first wave to N.5, Alpha, and Lambda in early 2021, and later to Gamma, Lambda, and Delta. Substitution rates were 2.4–6.8 × 10−4 substitutions/site/year. The findings highlight the value of genomic surveillance for timely public health responses.

title: Toward broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines: navigating viral evolution from past epidemics to future resilience

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on SARS-CoV-2, COVID-19, and its variants, with an emphasis on developing broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines that can address both current and future viral threats. The central question is how to create vaccines that are effective against multiple coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses, to enhance pandemic resilience.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of vaccine research on SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV prior to the COVID-19 outbreak, as well as vaccine development following the outbreak. It discusses strategies for broad-spectrum vaccine development and provides a perspective on future directions. The review does not explicitly report on databases, search dates, or meta-analysis methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that broad-spectrum vaccines are necessary to combat both currently circulating coronaviruses and those that may emerge in the future. It highlights the importance of understanding viral evolution and the need for vaccines that can provide cross-protection against related species.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that current approved vaccines offer strong protection against pre-Omicron variants but have reduced effectiveness against post-Omicron variants and limited cross-protection against other potential coronaviruses. This indicates a gap in vaccine efficacy against evolving strains and related viruses.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on developing vaccines that can provide broad-spectrum protection against multiple coronavirus species, including SARS-CoV-2 and related viruses. It emphasizes the need for strategies that account for viral evolution and enhance pandemic preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development of broad-spectrum coronavirus vaccines, emphasizing the need to address both current and future viral threats. It highlights the limitations of existing vaccines against post-Omicron variants and the importance of cross-protection against related species. The review discusses vaccine research on SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV before and after the COVID-19 outbreak, as well as strategies for creating vaccines that can combat multiple coronavirus species. It underscores the necessity of understanding viral evolution to improve pandemic resilience and vaccine effectiveness.

title: The role of personality traits in COVID-19 vaccination: A socio-cultural and gender-stratified analysis in Japan

analysis.scope_and_question: The review investigates the influence of personality traits on the uptake of the primary COVID-19 vaccination series in Japan, focusing on gender-specific patterns. The central question is whether personality traits, particularly the Big Five, act as psychological modifiers of vaccination behavior in this unique sociocultural context.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A web-based, cross-sectional survey was conducted among 7,210 Japanese adults aged 20–85 years in December 2021. Personality was assessed using the Japanese version of the Ten-Item Personality Inventory. Multivariable Poisson generalized estimating equations were used to calculate adjusted prevalence ratios (PRs) and assess gender–personality interactions.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Higher extraversion and lower openness were significantly associated with vaccination completion across genders. A significant gender–agreeableness interaction was observed: agreeableness was positively associated with vaccination completion among men but not women. A similar, though only marginally significant, interaction pattern was observed for neuroticism among men.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that the association between personality traits and vaccination behavior is context-dependent, as suggested by previous studies. However, the evidence is limited to Japan, and the gender-specific interactions require further validation in other populations.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Public health campaigns should transition from traditional “one-size-fits-all” messages to personality-tailored and gender-responsive communication strategies to optimize vaccine uptake and bolster psychological resilience in future pandemics.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the role of personality traits in influencing the uptake of the primary COVID-19 vaccination series in Japan, with a focus on gender-specific patterns. Using a cross-sectional survey of 7,210 Japanese adults, the study identifies higher extraversion and lower openness as significant predictors of vaccination completion across genders. A notable gender–agreeableness interaction is observed, where agreeableness positively correlates with vaccination completion in men but not women. Neuroticism also shows a marginally significant interaction pattern among men. The findings suggest that personality traits act as gender-specific psychological modifiers of vaccination behavior, highlighting the need for tailored public health communication strategies to enhance vaccine uptake and psychological resilience during future pandemics.

title: Genome-wide within-host evolution during prolonged SARS-CoV-2 infection in a person with advanced HIV infection

analysis.research_question_and_background: Within-host evolution during prolonged SARS-CoV-2 infection can be extensive in immunocompromised individuals, but the consequences of mutations that emerge and change in frequency over time remain difficult to predict.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We characterized an XBB.1.5.10 infection lasting nearly 90 days in a person with advanced human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) infection.
analysis.methods: Genome-wide tracking of allele frequencies in samples collected on study days 43, 48, and 70 revealed a Spike N-terminal domain (NTD) deletion spanning residues 138-145 at frequencies of 33%, 80%, and 96%, respectively.
analysis.main_results: A receptor-binding domain (RBD) deletion-insertion spanning residues 373-378 was detected on days 43 and 48 but not on day 70, while nsp12 C464Y was detected at approximately 8% on day 48 and 86% on day 70.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The representative Spike construct for days 43 and 48 increased entry relative to XBB.1.5.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Comparison with a matched construct lacking the receptor-binding domain deletion-insertion showed that the deletion-insertion enhanced entry, although it was not detected in the day 70 sample.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Together, allele-frequency tracking revealed both transient mutations and mutations detected at progressively higher frequencies across the sampled time points.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the within-host evolution of SARS-CoV-2 during a prolonged infection in a person with advanced HIV. The research highlights the extensive mutation patterns observed over nearly 90 days, including a Spike N-terminal domain deletion and a receptor-binding domain deletion-insertion. These mutations were tracked across different time points and showed varying frequencies. Functional testing indicated that increased entry or RNA replication in vitro did not always correlate with in vivo persistence. The findings contribute to understanding how mutations affect viral behavior in immunocompromised hosts, which has implications for surveillance and treatment strategies. However, the study's results are based on a single case, limiting generalizability and the strength of the evidence.

title: Recombinant Variants of SARS-CoV-2 Identified in the South of Western Siberia During the COVID-19 Pandemic

analysis.research_question_and_background: Recombination is one of the mechanisms driving SARS-CoV-2 evolution and can generate genomes with novel combinations of characteristics inherited from parental lineages.
analysis.study_design_and_population: We analyzed a total of 1963 SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences collected in the south of Western Siberia between March 2020 and 5 May 2023.
analysis.methods: Initial screening with Nextclade identified five potentially recombinant genomes. Recombinant origin was assessed with RecombinHunt and independently evaluated with 3SEQ and RDP5.
analysis.main_results: The consensus assemblies were re-examined by the originating laboratories and the absence of co-infection was confirmed. Recombination was confirmed for two sequences.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings indicate that automated classification should be followed by statistical validation, verification of genome assembly quality and the confirmed absence of co-infection.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Incomplete and uneven genomic surveillance may still limit reconstruction of the exact origins of rare recombinant variants.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: For EPI_ISL_15919275 the laboratory of origin did not confirm the reproducibility of the build. EPI_ISL_20438394 contained BA.2.35-like and XBB.3.1-like components but the signal did not survive correction for multiple comparisons.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the presence of recombinant variants of SARS-CoV-2 in the south of Western Siberia between March 2020 and May 2023. A total of 1963 genome sequences were analyzed, and initial screening with Nextclade identified five potentially recombinant genomes. Recombinant origin was assessed using RecombinHunt, 3SEQ, and RDP5. The consensus assemblies were re-examined to confirm the absence of co-infection. Recombination was confirmed for two sequences, while other potential recombinants were excluded due to lack of reproducibility or signal survival after multiple comparisons. The study highlights the importance of statistical validation and genome assembly quality verification in identifying recombinant variants. These findings suggest that genomic surveillance may need to be more comprehensive to accurately reconstruct the origins of rare recombinant variants.

title: Predictors of COVID-19 vaccination status among youth in eThekwini, South Africa: results from the AYAZAZI RIGHTS study.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Understanding which factors impact vaccine uptake is important for supporting ongoing and future vaccine programmes among youth. This study examined predictors of COVID-19 vaccination uptake among South African youth in the eThekwini District.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Cross-sectional data from an online survey (AYAZAZI RIGHTS: December 2021–May 2022) of youth aged 18–24 in the eThekwini district, South Africa, were analyzed. Of 1383 participants, 54% were women, with a median sample age of 21.8 years.
analysis.methods: A full model with backwards selection using Akaike’s Information Criterion was employed to remove predictors that did not add to the model’s explanatory power. The analysis used a gender-stratified logistic regression of vaccination status on candidate predictors of interest (k = 14).
analysis.main_results: In this cross‐sectional, observational analysis, the most consistent predictors of vaccination status were older age, living with seniors in the home, and personal proximity to severe pandemic outcomes, specifically knowing people who had been hospitalized or died due to COVID-19. Gender‐specific predictors included ethnicity, having children for women, employment, and relationship status.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Socio-demographic as well as community factors predicted receiving a COVID-19 vaccination, varying by gender. Better understanding of modifiable factors to support vaccine uptake, and curbing vaccine hesitancy related to mistrust and misinformation, will help support South Africa’s immunization programs among youth, and can help inform targeted, inclusive, and equity-oriented public-health strategies.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can help inform targeted, inclusive, and equity-oriented public-health strategies to support vaccine uptake among youth.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is cross-sectional, observational, and based on self-reported data, which may introduce bias and limit causal inference. The evidence is moderate as it is based on a single study with potential limitations in generalisability.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to identify predictors of COVID-19 vaccination status among youth in eThekwini, South Africa. A cross-sectional online survey conducted from December 2021 to May 2022 collected data from 1383 participants aged 18–24. The analysis used gender-stratified logistic regression to assess factors influencing vaccination uptake. Results showed that older age, living with seniors, and personal proximity to severe pandemic outcomes were the most consistent predictors. Gender-specific factors included ethnicity, having children, employment, and relationship status. The study highlights the importance of socio-demographic and community factors in vaccine uptake, suggesting that targeted strategies could improve immunization programs among youth. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal conclusions, and the evidence is moderate due to potential biases and limitations in generalisability.

title: Effects of XFG-adapted mRNA vaccination on SARS-CoV-2 variant neutralisation

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to assess the effects of XFG-adapted mRNA vaccination on SARS-CoV-2 variant neutralisation, as SARS-CoV-2 antigenic evolution continues to challenge strain-matched vaccination.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved 22 participants who received 30 μg of mRNA encoding XFG in September, 2026, with paired serum samples collected before vaccination and median 14 days after.
analysis.methods: The study used a pseudovirus assay to measure neutralising activity against various SARS-CoV-2 variants, including Wuhan-Hu-1, LP.8.1, NB.1.8.1, RV.1.3, PQ.16.1.1, XFG.1.1, and BA.3.2.2.
analysis.main_results: Median Wuhan-Hu-1 S1-specific IgG increased from 1600 BAU/mL (IQR 1118–2926) to 2914 BAU/mL (2117–4468), a 1·8-fold increase. Median RBD-binding ED50 increased from 116 (51·4–212) to 305·6 (170·8–434·6) for LP.8.1 and from 354·3 (129·2–558·2) to 832·9 (429–1175) for NB.1.8.1, corresponding to 2·6-fold and 2·4-fold increases, respectively (all p<0·0001). XFG-adapted vaccination increased neutralising activity against each tested variant. The GMT against XFG increased from 180 before vaccination to 894 afterwards (5·0-fold), and that against RV.1.3 increased from 121 to 599 (4·9-fold).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that XFG-adapted vaccination leads to a broad increase in neutralising activity against various SARS-CoV-2 variants, although post-vaccination neutralisation remained heterogeneous.

It focused on 22 participants who received the vaccine in September 2026 and had paired serum samples before and after vaccination. However, the study had limitations, including a small cohort, short follow-up, lack of a vaccine-comparator group, and the use of a pseudovirus assay. The findings suggest that XFG-adapted vaccination enhances neutralising activity against various SARS-CoV-2 variants, although post-vaccination neutralisation remained heterogeneous. title: Does COVID‐19 Vaccination Protect Against Post‐COVID Cardiovascular Conditions?

analysis.scope_and_question: Cardiovascular diseases, such as acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, have been associated with SARS‐CoV-2 infection, representing an important cause of long-term morbidity and mortality. This study aims to analyse the evidence supporting a causal relationship between COVID-19 vaccination and the prevention of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, based on classical and contemporary epidemiological criteria, including the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: A qualitative synthesis of the evidence was performed according to the nine BHC and the SCC model. The review includes evidence from the literature on the association between vaccination and post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, with a focus on epidemiological criteria.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Scientific evidence indicates that COVID-19 vaccination meets four of the nine BHC as a protective factor against post-COVID cardiovascular conditions, namely strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. The SCC model highlights the fundamental role of vaccination as a preventive causal component. It also contributes to two criteria, strength of association and temporality, while emphasising the limitation of specificity in causal inference.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Specificity and experimental evidence were not supported by the available literature. Additional studies are needed to explore the underlying biological mechanisms, interactions, and the role of COVID-19 vaccination in preventing post-COVID complications.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: COVID-19 vaccination has proven effective beyond the acute phase of the disease, with protection extending to a reduced risk of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions. Comprehensive immunisation strategies and reinfection prevention are essential to mitigate the burden of post-COVID conditions.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the evidence for a causal relationship between SARS-CoV-2 vaccination and the prevention of post-COVID cardiovascular conditions. Cardiovascular diseases, including acute myocardial infarction, heart failure, and arrhythmias, are significant long-term complications of SARS-CoV-2 infection. The study evaluates the Bradford Hill criteria (BHC) and the sufficient component cause (SCC) model to assess the protective role of vaccination. Evidence suggests that vaccination meets four of the nine BHC, including strength of association, consistency, temporality, and biological gradient. The SCC model underscores vaccination's role as a preventive causal component. However, the evidence lacks support for specificity and experimental validation. The review highlights the need for further research to explore biological mechanisms and interactions, as well as the importance of comprehensive immunisation strategies to reduce the burden of post-COVID conditions.

title: Wastewater‐Based Epidemiology for Monitoring SARS‐CoV‐2 Dynamics and Variants in Nagpur: Insights From a 16‐Month Study

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 dynamics and variants in Nagpur, India, during a 16-month period.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A longitudinal study was conducted from March 2023 to June 2024, collecting 1424 wastewater samples from 25 urban sites in Nagpur.
analysis.methods: Wastewater samples were tested for SARS-CoV-2 RNA, and 69 genomes were sequenced to identify viral lineages and variants, including prevalent VOIs like BA.2.86 and XBB.1.16.
analysis.main_results: 39% of the wastewater samples were positive for SARS-CoV-2 RNA, and sequencing revealed multiple lineages, including BA.2.86 and XBB.1.16, alongside lower abundance variants. No high-impact VOCs were detected.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study demonstrates that WBE can effectively track SARS-CoV-2 trends and variants, providing a complementary tool for surveillance. Unique local mutational patterns in ORF1ab and Spike genes were observed, indicating ongoing viral evolution.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings support the use of WBE for early outbreak detection and genomic surveillance, which can inform public health strategies and preparedness for future SARS-CoV-2 threats.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not find significant environmental factors influencing detection, and the evidence is moderate due to the observational nature of the study and potential limitations in sample representativeness.

analysis.summary_en: This 16-month study in Nagpur, India, evaluated wastewater-based epidemiology (WBE) for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 dynamics and variants. Wastewater samples were collected from 25 urban sites, with 39% testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 RNA. Sequencing of 69 genomes revealed multiple lineages, including BA.2.86 and XBB.1.16, but no high-impact VOCs were detected. The study found that viral concentrations correlated with clinical case trends, highlighting WBE as a useful surveillance tool. Unique local mutational patterns in ORF1ab and Spike genes were observed, suggesting ongoing viral evolution. The findings support the use of WBE for early outbreak detection and genomic surveillance, which can aid public health preparedness. However, the study did not find significant environmental influences on detection, and the evidence is considered moderate due to its observational design and potential limitations in sample representativeness.

title: Variation in social contact levels and changes during the COVID-19 pandemic by occupation and socio-economic status in east Zimbabwe

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to understand how social contact levels varied by occupation and socio-economic status during the COVID-19 pandemic in east Zimbabwe, as movement restrictions had uneven economic consequences in resource-constrained settings.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study used a population-representative survey (N=8,499) conducted in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, during April-May 2021, capturing typical weekday contacts before and during the first COVID-19 lockdown.
analysis.methods: Negative binomial regression models assessed pre-lockdown contact counts by socio-economic characteristics, overall and by place (home, school, work, transport, entertainment); linear regression assessed predictors of lockdown declines.
analysis.main_results: Pre-COVID-19, respondents reported a median of 12 daily contacts (interquartile range [IQR] 4-47), with higher counts among manual labourers, retail and public sector workers, students, males, wealthier respondents, under-30s, and urban and agricultural estate residents. Counts were highest in schools. During lockdown, contacts fell across all subgroups to a median of 8 (IQR 4-28). Declines were greatest among those with most pre-COVID-19 contacts: urban and agricultural estate residents, students and teachers, males and 30-44 year olds. Drops were greatest in schools and on transport.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as showing that reductions in contact under blanket lockdown varied markedly between subgroups and places in Manicaland, Zimbabwe, highlighting the need for targeted interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform public health strategies for reducing viral transmission in resource-constrained settings by identifying high-contact groups and places that could be prioritized for targeted interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on self-reported data and its focus on a single region in Zimbabwe, but the evidence is strong due to the use of regression models and a representative sample.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated variation in social contact levels and changes during the COVID-19 pandemic by occupation and socio-economic status in east Zimbabwe. It analyzed a population-representative survey of 8,499 individuals conducted during April-May 2021, capturing typical weekday contacts before and during the first lockdown. The results showed that pre-pandemic contact levels were higher among manual labourers, retail and public sector workers, students, males, wealthier individuals, under-30s, and urban and agricultural estate residents, with the highest counts observed in schools. During lockdown, contact levels decreased across all subgroups, with the most significant drops among those with the highest pre-lockdown contact levels, particularly in schools and transport. The authors concluded that targeted interventions for high-contact groups could achieve similar transmission reductions with less economic damage, offering insights for similar settings. The study's reliance on self-reported data and regional focus limits its generalizability, but the use of regression models and a representative sample supports its findings.

title: Demand Promotion Interventions to Improve COVID-19 Vaccine Uptake: A Systematic Review of the Global Evidence

analysis.scope_and_question: The review aimed to identify effective demand-side interventions to improve SARS-CoV-2 vaccine uptake globally, addressing challenges such as limited immunization infrastructure, shifting viral epidemiology, and vaccine misinformation. The central question focused on understanding the effectiveness of communication, behavioral, and health systems interventions in increasing vaccination demand and uptake.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Scopus, and Global Index Medicus from March 2022 to July 2024, including studies published after December 2020 with no language or geographic restrictions. Study quality was assessed using adapted Critical Appraisal Skills Program (CASP) criteria. Interventions were categorized into nine approaches based on an adapted communication and service-delivery taxonomy. A narrative synthesis combined with vote counting of studies with positive findings was used to evaluate intervention effectiveness.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review found that 70% of studies reported positive findings on at least one vaccination outcome. Educational interventions were most effective when delivered through multiple channels by trusted messengers and integrated with complementary strategies. Access-enhancing and service delivery interventions showed the most consistent evidence of effectiveness, with nine of ten studies reporting positive outcomes. Vaccine mandates had the strongest and most consistent effects on coverage at scale, though they raised ethical concerns.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Reminder and nudge interventions showed mixed results, performing best when embedded within multicomponent approaches. The review noted that most studies were conducted in high-income countries, leaving evidence gaps in low- and middle-income settings. There was also limited information on the effectiveness of interventions in specific population groups or regions.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Policymakers should prioritize access-enhancing and systems-strengthening interventions as a foundation, supplement these with targeted communication delivered by trusted messengers, and reserve mandate-based approaches for situations where less restrictive measures have proven insufficient. The findings also have relevance beyond the pandemic for adult immunization programs and future outbreak preparedness.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines demand-side interventions to improve SARS-CoV-2 vaccine uptake globally. It highlights the challenges of limited immunization infrastructure, shifting viral epidemiology, and vaccine misinformation. The review identifies educational, access-enhancing, and service delivery interventions as effective, with mandates showing strong effects but raising ethical concerns. Most studies were conducted in high-income countries, leaving gaps in low- and middle-income settings. The findings suggest a multi-component approach combining education, behavioral strategies, and improved access, with mandates used selectively. These insights are valuable for future outbreak preparedness and adult immunization programs.

title: Mental health and healthcare use during COVID‐19 among neurodivergent youth and youth with pre‐existing psychiatric disorders: A systematic review

analysis.scope_and_question: Neurodivergent youth and youth with pre‐existing psychiatric disorders may have faced additional challenges in navigating the demands and restrictions of the COVID‐19 pandemic. However, less is known about how mental health outcomes and psychiatric healthcare utilization differed across diagnostic groups and other youth‐related factors.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: We searched PubMed, Web of Science and additional sources for cross‐sectional and longitudinal studies with data collected between March 2020 and May 2023. Given the clinical and methodological diversity of studies, findings were synthesized narratively. Forty‐eight studies met the inclusion criteria. Most studies ( n = 40; 83.3%) had a moderate overall risk of bias (RoB), while seven (14.6%) had a high overall RoB.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Mental health outcomes showed mixed patterns both across and within diagnostic groups, with individual studies reporting symptom increase, stability and improvements. Mental health outcomes among youth with pre‐existing conditions during the COVID‐19 pandemic varied both within and across diagnostic groups. Outcomes were also associated with individual, developmental, contextual and service‐related factors.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: Evidence on psychiatric healthcare utilization was more limited and suggested different patterns between service use and psychotropic medication use. Evidence on psychiatric healthcare utilization remains limited.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: More methodologically robust research is needed to clarify mental health and healthcare‐use patterns during major public health emergencies.

analysis.summary_en: This systematic review examines mental health symptoms and psychiatric healthcare use among neurodivergent youth and those with pre-existing psychiatric disorders during the COVID-19 pandemic. The review includes 48 studies, with most having a moderate risk of bias. Mental health outcomes varied across and within diagnostic groups, showing mixed patterns of symptom increase, stability, and improvement. Evidence on healthcare utilization was limited, with differing patterns observed between service use and medication use. Girls were more likely to experience distress and increased service use compared to boys. Age-related findings varied across developmental stages and outcome domains. The review highlights the need for more robust research to better understand these patterns during public health emergencies.

title: Data Reduction in SARS-CoV-2 Amplicon Sequencing: Effects of Read Subsampling and Normalization on Consensus Quality, Lineage Assignment, and Computational Burden

analysis.research_question_and_background: Amplicon-based next-generation sequencing is a cornerstone of viral genomic surveillance, but it often produces datasets with highly uneven read coverage due to PCR amplification bias.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This leads to excessive data generation and substantial computational overhead for downstream bioinformatic analysis.
analysis.methods: Results We evaluated the efficacy of two data reduction strategies on 220 SARS-CoV-2 clinical specimens and 12 wastewater samples: random subsampling with SeqKit and read depth normalization with BBNorm.
analysis.main_results: FASTQ files were reduced to target depths from 10X to 10,000X to compare genome coverage, lineage assignment concordance, and computational resource usage.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Both strategies markedly reduced total processing time.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: For clinical isolates, read depth normalization corrected for amplification bias resulting in highly concordant lineage assignments at a target depth of just 200X.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: However, aggressive data reduction should be avoided in environmental surveillance, where maintaining a high baseline sequencing depth is critical for accurate mixed-variant deconvolution.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the effects of data reduction strategies on SARS-CoV-2 amplicon sequencing, focusing on how read subsampling and normalization impact consensus quality, lineage assignment, and computational burden. The research evaluates two methods—random subsampling with SeqKit and read depth normalization with BBNorm—on 220 clinical specimens and 12 wastewater samples, reducing FASTQ files to target depths from 10X to 10,000X. Both methods significantly reduced processing time, with read depth normalization achieving accurate lineage assignments at 200X depth for clinical isolates, while random subsampling required depths over 500X. However, in wastewater samples, reducing depths below 500X severely degraded variant deconvolution accuracy. The authors conclude that the optimal method depends on the analytical goal, with random subsampling suitable for rapid lineage assignment and read depth normalization preferred for high-quality consensus sequences. They caution against aggressive data reduction in environmental surveillance due to the risk of inaccurate variant detection.

title: Epidemiology and virological characteristics of the emerging SARS-CoV-2 variant PJ.2.1

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to characterize a new SARS-CoV-2 variant, PJ.2.1, and its epidemiological and virological features, addressing the ongoing evolution of SARS-CoV-2 variants globally.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved a brief characterization of PJ.2.1 and other circulating variants in the USA, Canada, and Spain, focusing on epidemiological and virological aspects.
analysis.methods: The study utilized epidemiological data and virological assays to characterize PJ.2.1 and other variants, including sequencing and antibody inhibition assays.
analysis.main_results: PJ.2.1 was found to spread in the USA, Canada, and Spain, predominantly infecting older individuals, with reduced susceptibility to an ACE2-targeting antibody but not to antibodies from vaccinees.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that PJ.2.1's increased affinity for ACE2 rather than enhanced antibody evasion may drive its rapid spread.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results provide insights into the epidemiological and virological characteristics of PJ.2.1, which can inform surveillance and public health strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's limitations include its brief nature and the need for further research to confirm the findings, with a moderate assessment of evidence strength.

analysis.summary_en: This study characterized the new SARS-CoV-2 variant PJ.2.1, showing it spreads predominantly in older individuals and has reduced susceptibility to certain antibodies, suggesting increased ACE2 affinity drives its spread.

title: Anesthesia as a Partner in Public Health: Enabling National Pediatric SARS-CoV-2 Serosurveillance in Australia

analysis.scope_and_question: Anesthetic departments played a critical role in Australia’s COVID-19 response by facilitating the collection of residual blood samples from children undergoing elective procedures.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: Through a partnership with the Pediatric Active Enhanced Disease Surveillance network, this approach enabled three national SARS-CoV-2 serosurveys between 2020 and 2023.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: It provided an ethical, feasible, and nationally representative method for assessing infection- and vaccine-derived immunity in children, a population in whom routine blood sampling is difficult and from whom residual blood samples are not commonly available.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The resulting data informed COVID-19 vaccination policy, improved understanding of infection burden and immunity, and contributed to broader public health decision-making.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: This experience demonstrates how anesthetic departments can extend their impact beyond perioperative care, serving as essential partners in public health surveillance and research.

analysis.summary_en: This review highlights the role of anesthetic departments in Australia’s response to SARS-CoV-2 by facilitating the collection of residual blood samples from children undergoing elective procedures. This approach enabled three national SARS-CoV-2 serosurveys between 2020 and 2023, providing an ethical, feasible, and nationally representative method for assessing infection- and vaccine-derived immunity in children. The data from these surveys informed vaccination policy, improved understanding of infection burden and immunity, and contributed to broader public health decision-making. The study demonstrates how anesthetic departments can extend their impact beyond perioperative care, serving as essential partners in public health surveillance and research.

title: Prognostic implications of asymptomatic COVID-19 infection in non-small-cell lung cancer patients receiving active anticancer treatment: an observational study with prospective survival follow-up.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to evaluate the survival outcomes of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with or without COVID-19 infection during the Omicron variant attack between January and April 2022, as NSCLC was previously reported as a significant predictor of delayed viral clearance.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This prospective cohort study included 276 NSCLC patients recruited, of whom 39 were SARS-CoV-2 positive through PCR testing, with viral load indicated by cycle threshold (ct) values.
analysis.methods: Propensity score matching was used to ensure the COVID-positive and COVID-negative groups were comparable in demographics, disease staging, and treatment modalities. Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression were performed to evaluate overall survival and identify OS prognostic factors.
analysis.main_results: After a median follow up of 39.9 months from diagnosis, 20 died of COVID-19 and NSCLC. OS differences counting from either their NSCLC diagnosis or the start of anticancer treatment were insignificant among various stages of NSCLC patients infected with COVID-19, but they were significant for COVID-negative patients (P = 0.050 and P = 0.009, respectively). Exploratory analysis revealed that ct value cutoff of > 34.14 correlated with a better OS (P = 0.039).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted that asymptomatic COVID-19 infection might compromise survival outcomes of NSCLC patients in this study, highlighting the need for closer attention to this population.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection may have prognostic implications for NSCLC patients undergoing active anticancer treatment, potentially informing future surveillance and risk assessment strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its observational design and potential confounding factors, but the evidence is strong due to the use of propensity score matching and survival analysis methods.

analysis.summary_en: This observational study investigated the survival outcomes of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients with or without asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection during the Omicron variant attack in 2022. A prospective cohort of 276 NSCLC patients was followed for a median of 39.9 months, with 39 testing positive for SARS-CoV-2 via PCR. Propensity score matching was used to compare groups, and survival analysis revealed that OS differences were significant for COVID-negative patients but not for those infected with SARS-CoV-2. Exploratory analysis suggested a ct value cutoff of > 34.14 correlated with better OS. The authors concluded that asymptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection may negatively impact survival outcomes in NSCLC patients, emphasizing the need for closer monitoring. The study's evidence is moderate due to its observational nature, though the use of matching and survival analysis strengthens its validity.

title: SARS-CoV-2-Specific IgG Levels Are Inversely Associated with ACPA-Reactive Pathological and Natural Autoantibody Profiles in Residual Diagnostic Samples

analysis.research_question_and_background: Background/Objectives: SARS-CoV-2-specific antibody levels vary among patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs).
analysis.study_design_and_population: In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the most prevalent SARD, this is further shaped by rheumatoid factors (RFs).
analysis.methods: A decade-long dataset (2014–2024; 73,747 patients) gave descriptive context, not the substudy population. SARS-CoV-2 IgG and nAAbs were evaluated in 200 residual specimens collected between November 2023 and February 2024. SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG was interpreted as an antiviral readout, not a protection correlate (clinical/exposure data unavailable).
analysis.main_results: ACPA-reactive samples showed lower antiviral IgG across both assays. After age/sex adjustment, comparator groups had 2.58–3.30-fold higher QuantiVac and 2.70–4.87-fold higher Omicron BA.1 IgG. Antiviral IgG correlated inversely with ACPA IgG (ρ to −0.474) and RF isotypes (ρ = −0.299 to −0.400). ACPA-reactive samples showed increased CS-IgM and HSP60/HSP70 IgG/IgM reactivity, which correlated positively with ACPA IgG and RF isotypes.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: In this exploratory analysis, an ACPA-reactive serological profile was associated with lower SARS-CoV-2 IgG and higher, positively correlated CS- and HSP-directed autoantibody levels, suggesting a shared rather than independent basis for these autoreactive compartments.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Attenuated post-vaccination antibody levels in RA are documented, but links to broader autoreactivity remain underexplored.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These cross-sectional associations persisted after age/sex adjustment but cannot be separated from unmeasured clinical, treatment, or exposure factors.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the relationship between SARS-CoV-2-specific IgG levels and autoantibody profiles in patients with systemic autoimmune rheumatic diseases (SARDs), particularly rheumatoid arthritis (RA). The research highlights that ACPA-reactive samples exhibit lower antiviral IgG levels compared to other groups, with significant inverse correlations observed between SARS-CoV-2 IgG and ACPA IgG or RF isotypes. The findings suggest a potential shared basis for these autoreactive compartments rather than independent mechanisms. However, the study acknowledges limitations, as the cross-sectional associations may be influenced by unmeasured clinical, treatment, or exposure factors. The results contribute to understanding the interplay between SARS-CoV-2 immunity and autoantibody profiles in RA, offering insights into the complex immune responses in autoimmune conditions.
